Commentary on Surah Fatir

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

* *

Sufyan al-Thawri narrated from Ibrahim ibn Muhajir, from Mujahid, from Ibn Abbas, who said: "I did not know what (fatir) of the heavens and the earth meant until two Bedouins came to me disputing over a well. One of them said to his companion: 'I am the one who originated it (fatartuha), I began it.'" Then Ibn Abbas said: ﴿Originator of the heavens and the earth﴾, meaning the Innovator (badi') of the heavens and the earth. [Narrated by al-Bayhaqi in Shu'ab al-Iman, no. 1682, through Yahya ibn Sa'id from Sufyan with this chain.]

And al-Dahhak said: "Everything in the Qur'an that reads fatir al-samawat wal-ard means: Creator (khaliq) of the heavens and the earth."

* *

As for His words: ﴿Who made the angels messengers﴾, meaning between Himself and His prophets, ﴿possessing wings﴾, meaning they fly with them to convey swiftly what they have been commanded, ﴿two, or three, or four﴾, meaning some of them have two wings, some have three, some have four, and some have more than that. As has come in the hadith that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) saw Jibril on the night of the Isra' having six hundred wings, between every two wings the distance of what lies between the east and the west. Therefore He said: ﴿He increases in creation what He wills. Indeed, Allah is over all things competent.﴾ Al-Suddi said: "He increases in the wings and their creation what He wills."

Al-Zuhri and Ibn Juraij said, regarding His words ﴿He increases in creation what He wills﴾, that it means the beauty of the voice. This was narrated from al-Zuhri by al-Bukhari in al-Adab al-Mufrad, and by Ibn Abi Hatim in his Tafsir.

It was also read in the irregular (shadhdh) reading: "yazid fi al-halq", with the unmarked ha' (ح), and Allah knows best.

Ibn Kathir (may Allah have mercy on him) said:

He, may He be exalted, informs that whatever He wills comes to be, and whatever He does not will does not come to be; that there is none who can withhold what He gives, and none who can give what He withholds.

[Variant: "وروي" ("It is also narrated") instead of "قال" ("said").] Imam Ahmad said: Ali ibn Asim narrated to us, Mughirah narrated to us, Amir informed us, from Warrad, the freedman of al-Mughirah ibn Shu'bah, who said: Mu'awiyah wrote to al-Mughirah ibn Shu'bah: "Write to me what you have heard from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ)." So al-Mughirah summoned me, and I wrote to him: "I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), when he finished the prayer, say: 'There is no god but Allah alone, with no partner. To Him belongs the dominion and to Him belongs all praise, and He is capable of all things. O Allah, there is none who can withhold what You have given, and none who can give what You have withheld, and the might of the mighty person does not benefit him against You (lit. wealth/fortune does not benefit its owner from You).'" And I heard him forbid "qil wa qal" (gossip), excessive questioning, the squandering of wealth, burying daughters alive, disobedience to mothers, and "man' wa hat" (withholding and demanding).

[Variant: "سمعت من" in one manuscript, "سمعت" in the text.] Al-Bukhari and Muslim both narrated it through various chains from Warrad, with the same wording.

Sahih Muslim also authentically narrates from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri (may Allah be pleased with him) that when the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) raised his head from bowing, he would say: "Allah hears whoever praises Him. Our Lord, to You belongs all praise, filling the heavens and the earth, and filling whatever else You will after that. O Allah, Possessor of praise and glory, the truest thing a servant says, and we are all Your servants. O Allah, there is none who can withhold what You have given, and none who can give what You have withheld, and the might of the mighty person does not benefit him against You."

[Variant: "وملء الأرض" ("and filling the earth") in some manuscripts.] [Sahih Muslim, no. 477.] [Variant: "ولهما" ("and for both of them") in one manuscript, "ولها" in another.]

This verse is like His saying: ﴿And if Allah touches you with adversity, there is none to remove it except Him; and if He intends for you good, there is none to repel His bounty﴾ [Yunus: 107]. There are many similar examples of this.

Imam Malik said: Abu Hurairah, whenever it rained, would say: "We have been rained upon by the star of the opening (nawʾ al-fath)," then he would recite this verse: ﴿Whatever mercy Allah grants to people, none can withhold it; and whatever He withholds, none can release it after Him. And He is the Almighty, the All-Wise﴾. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it from Yunus, from Ibn Wahb, from him.

[Variant: "بالعبادة وحده" ("in worship alone") in one manuscript.]

Almighty Allah admonishes His servants and guides them to deduce His Oneness by singling Him out in worship. Just as He alone is the Creator and the Provider, likewise He alone should be worshipped, and no one else should be associated with Him, whether idols, rivals (al-andad) or images (al-awthan). For this reason He said: ﴿There is no deity except Him, so how are you deluded?﴾ That is, how are you turned away (tu'faku) after this clarification and this clear proof, and yet after all this you worship rivals and images?

He says: "And if these polytheists deny you, O Muhammad, and oppose you regarding the monotheism (tawhid, the affirmation of God's oneness) that you have brought them, then you have an example in the messengers who came before you. They likewise came to their peoples with clear proofs and commanded them to worship God alone, but their peoples denied them and opposed them. ﴿And to God all matters are returned﴾, meaning: We will repay them for that with the fullest recompense."

Then He said: ﴿O mankind, indeed the promise of God is true﴾, meaning the Resurrection (ma'ad, the return) will certainly take place. ﴿So let not the worldly life deceive you﴾, meaning the lowly livelihood of this world, compared to the great good that God has prepared for His friends and for the followers of His messengers. So do not become distracted from that which endures by this fading blossom. ﴿And let not the Deceiver deceive you concerning God﴾. The Deceiver is Satan, said Ibn 'Abbas. That is: let Satan not tempt you and turn you away from following the messengers of God and believing His words, for he is a constant deceiver, a great liar and a grave sinner.

This verse is like the verse at the end of Surah Luqman: ﴿So let not the worldly life deceive you, and let not the Deceiver deceive you concerning God﴾ [Luqman: 33]. Malik related from Zayd ibn Aslam: "It is Satan." This is like His saying: The believers will say to the hypocrites on the Day of Resurrection, when a wall is set up between them with a gate, its inner side containing mercy and its outer side facing the torment: ﴿They will call out to them, "Were we not with you?" They will say, "Yes, but you tempted yourselves, waited, doubted, and false hopes deluded you until the command of God came, and the Deceiver deceived you concerning God."﴾ [al-Hadid: 13–14].

Then God made clear the enmity of Iblis toward the children of Adam, saying: ﴿Indeed, Satan is an enemy to you, so take him as an enemy.﴾ That is: he openly opposes you with enmity, so you must oppose him with the utmost enmity, contradict him, and reject what he deceives you with. ﴿He only invites his party so that they may be among the companions of the Blaze﴾. That is: he only intends to lead you astray until you enter with him into the torment of the Blaze. This is the clear enemy. So we ask God, the Strong, the Mighty, to make us enemies of Satan, to grant us the following of His Book and the emulation of the way of His Messenger (ﷺ). Indeed He is capable of whatever He wills, and worthy of answering. This is like His saying: ﴿And when We said to the angels, "Prostrate to Adam," they prostrated, except Iblis. He was of the jinn and defied the command of his Lord. Will you then take him and his offspring as allies instead of Me, while they are an enemy to you? Evil is the exchange for the wrongdoers.﴾ [al-Kahf: 50].

[Some scholars said: Beneath this address lies a subtle kind of reproach, as if He were saying: "I opposed Iblis for the sake of your father and for your sake. How then is it fitting for you to take him as an ally? Rather, what befits you is to oppose him, contradict him, and not obey him."]

Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 35, verses 9–11 (part 1 of 2):

Very often, Allah (exalted is He) argues for the Resurrection by His giving life to the earth after its death, as in the beginning of Surah al-Hajj [[addition from manuscripts T, S, A.]]. He alerts His servants to take a lesson from this regarding that matter. The earth is dead and lifeless, with no vegetation in it. Then, when He sends the clouds carrying water down onto it [[in manuscript T: "upon it".]] and sends the water down upon it, ﴿it stirs, swells, and produces every lovely kind of growth﴾ [al-Hajj: 5]. Likewise the bodies, when Allah (glorified is He) wills to resurrect them and raise them, He sends down rain from beneath the Throne that covers the whole earth, and the bodies grow in their graves just as seeds grow in the earth. For this reason it is reported in the Sahih: "Every son of Adam decays except the coccyx bone (ʿajb al-dhanab), from it he was created and from it he will be reassembled." For this reason Allah (exalted is He) said: ﴿Thus will be the resurrection﴾.

The hadith of Abu Razin was mentioned in al-Hajj [[at the verses 12–16.]]: I said, "O Messenger of Allah, how does Allah give life to the dead, and what is the sign of that in His creation?" He said: "O Abu Razin, did you not pass by the valley of your people when it was barren [[in manuscripts T, S, A: "parched".]], then you passed by it again and it was stirring green?" I said, "Yes." He said: "So likewise Allah gives life to the dead."

* *

His saying: ﴿Whoever desires honour—to Allah belongs all honour﴾. That is: whoever loves to be honoured in this world and the Hereafter, let him adhere to the obedience of Allah, for he will attain his aim, because Allah is the Owner of this world and the Hereafter, and all honour belongs to Him, as He (exalted is He) said: ﴿Those who take the disbelievers as allies instead of the believers—do they seek honour with them? Indeed, all honour belongs to Allah﴾ [al-Nisa': 139].

And He (exalted is He) said: ﴿And let not their saying grieve you. Indeed, all honour belongs to Allah﴾ [Yunus: 65], and He said: ﴿Honour belongs to Allah, His Messenger, and the believers, but the hypocrites do not know﴾ [al-Munafiqun: 8].

Mujahid said: ﴿Whoever desires honour﴾ [by worshipping idols], ﴿then indeed, all honour belongs to Allah﴾.

Qatadah said: ﴿Whoever desires honour, then to Allah belongs all honour﴾. That is: let him seek honour through obedience to Allah, Mighty and Majestic.

It was also said: "Whoever desires the knowledge of honour, to whom it belongs—﴿indeed, all honour belongs to Allah﴾." This was related by Ibn Jarir.

* *

His saying: ﴿To Him ascends the good word﴾. It means: the remembrance (dhikr), the recitation, and the supplication. This was said by more than one of the early generations (al-salaf).

Ibn Jarir said: Muhammad ibn Isma'il al-Ahmasi related to me, Ja'far ibn Awn informed me, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abd Allah al-Mas'udi, from Abd Allah ibn al-Mukhariq, from his father al-Mukhariq ibn Sulaym, who said: Abd Allah (that is, Ibn Mas'ud) said to us: "When we narrate a hadith to you, we bring you its confirmation from the Book of Allah: indeed, when the Muslim servant says, 'Glory be to Allah and praise be to Him, and all praise is for Allah, there is no god but Allah, Allah is greatest, blessed is Allah,' an angel takes them and places them beneath his wing, then he ascends with them to the heaven. He does not pass with them by any group of angels except that they seek forgiveness for the one who said them, until he brings them before the Face of the Most Merciful, Mighty and Majestic." Then Abd Allah recited: ﴿To Him ascends the good word, and righteous deed raises it﴾.

And Ya'qub ibn Ibrahim related to me: Ibn Ulayyah narrated to us, Sa'id al-Juraydi informed us, from Abd Allah ibn Shaqiq, who said: Ka'b al-Ahbar said: "Indeed, for 'Glory be to Allah, all praise is for Allah, there is no god but Allah, and Allah is greatest' there is a humming around the Throne like the humming of bees, mentioning their companion. And the righteous deed is in the treasuries." [Tafsir al-Tabari (22/80).]

This is a sound chain (isnad) up to Ka'b al-Ahbar, may Allah have mercy on him, and it has also been related in a marfu' form (traced to the Prophet).

Imam Ahmad said: Ibn Numayr narrated to us, Musa—meaning Ibn Muslim al-Tahhan—narrated to us, from Awn ibn Abd Allah, from his father—or his brother—from al-Nu'man ibn Bashir, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Those who mention the Majesty of Allah, through His glorification, His magnification, His praise, and His declaration of His oneness (tahlil), they encircle the Throne, and they have a humming like the humming of bees, mentioning their companion. For this reason He said: ﴿For them is a severe punishment, and the plotting of those—it will perish﴾, that is: it will be corrupted, it will be nullified, and their falsehood will become apparent soon to those of insight and sound intellect. Indeed, no servant conceals a secret except that Allah makes it appear upon the surfaces of his face and the slips of his tongue, and no one conceals a secret except that Allah clothes him in its garment: if it is good, then it is good, and if it is evil, then it is evil. So the show-off's affair does not sell and does not persist except among the foolish. As for the believers who have discernment, it does not pass on them, rather it is uncovered to them soon, and the Knower of the Unseen, nothing is hidden from Him.

* *

His saying: ﴿And Allah created you from dust, then from a drop of semen﴾. That is: He began the creation of your father Adam from dust, then made his progeny from an extract of despised water, ﴿then He made you into pairs﴾, that is, male and female, out of His kindness and mercy, when He made for you mates of your own kind, so that you might find tranquility in them.

* *

His saying: ﴿No female conceives or gives birth except with His knowledge﴾. That is: He knows that, and nothing of it is hidden from Him. Rather, ﴿not a leaf falls but He knows it, nor a grain in the darknesses of the earth, nor anything fresh or dry, but it is in a clear Record﴾ [al-An'am: 59]. The discussion of His saying was already given: ﴿Allah knows what every female bears, and what the wombs diminish and what they increase; and everything with Him is by measure. Knower of the unseen and the witnessed, the Great, the Exalted﴾ [al-Ra'd: 8–9] [[addition from manuscripts T, S, A; in manuscript H: "up to His saying".]].

* *

His saying: ﴿And no one is granted a long life, nor is any of his life shortened, except that it is in a Record﴾. That is: what is given to some drops of length of life, He knows it, and it is in the Primordial Book with Him. ﴿Nor is any of his life shortened﴾: the pronoun refers to the category (jins), not to the individual person, because the individual's long life is in the Book and in Allah's knowledge, and it is not shortened. The pronoun refers to the category.

Ibn Jarir said: This is like their saying, "I have a garment and its half," meaning: and another half.

It is related through al-Awfi from Ibn Abbas regarding His saying: ﴿And no one is granted a long life, nor is any of his life shortened, except that it is in a Record. Indeed that is easy for Allah﴾, he said: "No one for whom I have decreed a long life and existence, but he will reach what I have decreed for him of life, and I have decreed that for him. He only comes to the Record that I have decreed, which is not increased. And no one for whom I have decreed a short life and existence will reach a longer life, but he comes to the Record that I wrote for him. That is His saying: ﴿nor is any of his life shortened, except that it is in a Record. Indeed that is easy for Allah﴾, meaning: all of that is in a Record with Him."

Likewise said al-Dahhak ibn Muzahim.

Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam said, from his father: ﴿Nor is any of his life shortened, except that it is in a Record﴾: "It is the wombs that expel children without completion."

Abd al-Rahman said in explaining it: "Do you not see people? A man lives a hundred years, and another dies as soon as he is born. This is that."

Qatadah said: "What is shortened from his life is that one who dies before sixty years."

Mujahid said: ﴿And no one is granted a long life, nor is any of his life shortened, except that it is in a Record﴾, that is: in his mother's womb it is written for him. He did not create creatures with one lifespan; rather, for this one there is a lifespan, and for this one there is a lifespan that is shorter than his, and all of it is written for its owner, whatever it reaches.

Some of them said: Rather, its meaning is: ﴿no one is granted a long life﴾, that is: what is written of the term, ﴿nor is any of his life shortened﴾, and that is its passing little by little, all of it known to Allah: year after year, month after month, week after week, day after day, hour after hour, all of it written with Allah in a Record.

Ibn Jarir related this from Abu Malik, and al-Suddi and Ata al-Khurasani went to it. Ibn Jarir preferred the first view, and it is as he said.

al-Nasa'i said, when explaining this noble verse: Ahmad ibn Yahya ibn Abi Zayd ibn Sulayman narrated to us, I heard Ibn Wahb say: Yunus narrated to me, from Ibn Shihab, from Anas ibn Malik, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: "Whoever would like his provision to be expanded for him, and his life (athar) to be extended for him, let him maintain his ties of kinship."

It was related by al-Bukhari, Muslim, and Abu Dawud, from the hadith of Yunus ibn Yazid al-Aylli, with the same wording. [al-Nasa'i in al-Sunan al-Kubra, no. 11429; Sahih al-Bukhari, no. 2067; Sahih Muslim, no. 2557; Sunan Abi Dawud, no. 1693.]

Ibn Abi Hatim [[in manuscript T: "and related".]] said: Ali ibn al-Husayn narrated to us, al-Walid ibn Abd al-Malik ibn Ubayd Allah Abu Musarrih narrated to us, Uthman ibn Ata narrated to us, from Maslamah ibn Abd Allah, from his paternal uncle Abu Mash'a ibn Rib'i [[in manuscript A: "Salamah".]], from Abu al-Darda', may Allah be pleased with him, who said: We mentioned it in the presence of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and he said: "Indeed Allah does not delay a soul when its term has come. The increase of life is only through a righteous offspring that a servant is granted, and they supplicate for him after him, and their supplication reaches him in his grave; that is the increase of life."

* *

Allah's saying: ﴿Indeed, that is easy for Allah﴾ means: it is easy for Him, and His knowledge of that and of its details among all His creatures is effortless for Him, for His knowledge encompasses all of that, and nothing of it is hidden from Him.

Allah, exalted is He, says, drawing attention to His great power in creating different things: "And He created the two seas, the sweet and palatable (al-'adhb al-zulal), which are these rivers flowing among the people, large and small, according to the need for them in the regions and cities, the inhabited lands, the deserts and the wastelands. Their drink is sweet and pleasant for whoever wishes it. ﴿And this one is salty and bitter﴾, which is the still sea upon which large ships sail. Its water is only salty, brackish and bitter, and for this reason He said: ﴿And this one is salty and bitter﴾, meaning bitter."

Then He said: ﴿And from both you eat fresh tender flesh﴾, meaning fish, ﴿and you extract ornaments which you wear﴾, as He said elsewhere: ﴿From them emerge the pearls and the coral. So which of the favours of your Lord would you deny?﴾ [Ar-Rahman: 22, 23].

* *

As for His saying: ﴿And you see the ships therein plowing (mawakhir)﴾ [[In manuscripts T and S: "And you see the ships plowing therein." Perhaps they meant the verse 14 of Surah An-Nahl.]], meaning: they cut through it and split it with their prows (hayzuwmuha), which is their forward part, the raised one that resembles the breast of a bird (judu'ju al-tayr), which is its chest.

Mujahid said: "The wind plows the ships, and only the large ships are plowed by the wind."

* *

As for His saying: ﴿that you may seek of His bounty﴾, meaning: through your journeys for trade, from one land to another and from one region to another, ﴿and perhaps you will be grateful﴾, meaning you will thank your Lord for subjecting to you this great creation, which is the sea, that you may dispose of it as you wish and go wherever you desire, and nothing from it is out of your reach. Rather, by His power He has subjected to you what is in the heavens and what is on the earth, all of it from His bounty and His mercy.

This is also from His perfect power and great dominion, in His subjecting the night with its darkness and the day with its light. He takes from the length of this and adds it to the shortness of that, so that the two become equal. Then He takes from this and gives to that, so this lengthens and that shortens. Then they alternate with each other in summer and winter. ﴿And He has subjected the sun and the moon﴾, that is, and the wandering stars and the piercing stars with their lights, the celestial bodies, all of them moving at a determined measure and along a fixed, precisely arranged course, by the decree of the Mighty, the All-Knowing.

﴿Each runs for a specified term﴾, that is, until the Day of Resurrection.

﴿That is Allah, your Lord﴾, that is: the One who did this is the great Lord, there is no god besides Him. ﴿And those you invoke besides Him﴾, that is, the rivals and idols, which are in the likeness of those you claim to be the angels brought near, ﴿do not possess even a qiṭmīr﴾.

Ibn ʿAbbas, Mujahid, ʿIkrimah, ʿAṭāʾ, ʿAṭiyyah al-ʿAwfi, al-Hasan, Qatadah and others said: al-Qiṭmīr is the thin membrane that covers the date-stone (nawāt al-tamrah). That is, they do not own anything of the heavens and the earth, not even the measure of this qiṭmīr.

Then He said: ﴿If you call upon them, they will not hear your call﴾, meaning: the deities you invoke besides Allah do not hear your call, because they are lifeless objects with no spirits in them. ﴿And even if they heard, they would not respond to you﴾, that is, they are not able to do what you ask of them. ﴿And on the Day of Resurrection they will disavow your association﴾, that is, they will disown you, as Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And who is more astray than one who calls upon other than Allah those who will not respond to him until the Day of Resurrection, and they are unaware of their calling? And when the people are gathered, they will be enemies to them and will deny their worship﴾ [al-Ahqaf: 5–6], and He said: ﴿And they have taken besides Allah gods, that they might be for them a source of honor. No! They will reject their worship and will be against them opponents﴾ [Maryam: 81–82].

* *

His saying: ﴿If He wills, He can take you away and bring a new creation﴾, meaning: if He willed, He would take you away, O people, and bring a people other than you. This is not difficult for Him or impossible. For this reason He says: ﴿And that is not difficult for Allah﴾.

* *

His saying: ﴿No bearer of burdens will bear the burden of another﴾, meaning on the Day of Resurrection. ﴿And if a heavily laden soul calls [another] to its load﴾, meaning if a soul weighed down by its sins calls someone to help it bear some or all of the sins upon it, ﴿nothing of it will be carried, even if he were a relative﴾, meaning even if he were close to it, even if he were its father or its son. Each is preoccupied with himself and his own condition, [as He, may He be exalted, said: ﴿On the day a man flees from his brother, and his mother and his father, and his spouse and his children, each man that day will have a matter sufficient to occupy him﴾] [Abasa: 34-37]. [[Addition from manuscript T.]]

Ikrimah said regarding His saying: ﴿And if a heavily laden soul calls [another] to its load﴾, up to the end of the verse: He said, "It refers to a neighbour who clings to his neighbour on the Day of Resurrection, saying: 'O Lord, ask this one why he used to close his door against me.' And the disbeliever clings to the believer on the Day of Resurrection, saying to him: 'O believer, I have a favour upon you. You know how I was to you in the world, and I am now in need of you today.' The believer will continue to intercede for him with his Lord until He returns him to a station below his station, while he is in the Fire. And the father clings to his son on the Day of Resurrection, saying: 'O my son, what a father was I to you?' He praises him with goodness, and so he says to him: 'O my son, I am in need of an atom's weight of your good deeds by which I may be saved from what you see.' His son says to him: 'O father, how easy is what you have asked, but I fear what you fear, and I am not able to give you anything.' Then he clings to his wife and says: 'O so-and-so, or O this one, what a husband was I to you?' She praises him with goodness, and so he says to her: 'I ask of you one good deed that you may grant me, perhaps I may be saved by it from what you see.' She says: 'How easy is what you have asked. But I cannot give you anything, for I fear what you fear.' Allah says: ﴿And if a heavily laden soul calls [another] to its load﴾, the verse, and Allah says: ﴿No parent will avail anything for his child, nor will a child avail anything for his parent﴾ [Luqman: 33], and He, may He be exalted, says: ﴿On the day a man flees from his brother and his mother and his father and his spouse and his children, each man that day will have a matter sufficient to occupy him﴾."

Ibn Abi Hatim, may Allah have mercy on him, narrated it from Abu Abdullah al-Tahrani [[In manuscript A: "al-Tabarani".]], from Hafs ibn Umar, from al-Hakam ibn Aban, from Ikrimah, with it.

**Ibn Kathir's commentary on verses 27–28 of Surah Fatir (35)**

God, exalted is He, draws attention to the perfection of His power in creating varied and differing things from one single substance, which is the water He sends down from the sky. By it He brings forth fruits of differing colours: yellow, red, green, white, and other colours of fruit. This is what is observed in the variety of their colours, flavours and fragrances. As He says in another verse: ﴿And on the earth are adjoining tracts, and gardens of vines, and crops, and palm trees, some multi-stemmed and some single-stemmed, watered with one water. Yet We make some of them exceed others in fruit. Indeed in that are signs for a people who reason.﴾ [Ar-Ra'd: 4].

* *

His saying, blessed and exalted is He: ﴿And among the mountains are streaks, white and red, of varying shades, and some are intensely black.﴾ That is, He created the mountains likewise, of differing colours, as is also observed: white and red. In some of them there are streaks (*tara'iq*), which are the *judad* (streaks, the plural of *judda*), of differing colours too.

Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with both of them, said: *al-judad* are the streaks (*tara'iq*). Abu Malik, al-Hasan, Qatadah and as-Suddi said likewise.

Among them is ﴿and intensely black﴾. 'Ikrimah said: *al-gharabib* are the tall black mountains. Abu Malik, 'Ata' al-Khurasani and Qatadah also said likewise.

Ibn Jarir said: when the Arabs describe a black thing as having much blackness, they say: *aswad ghirbib* (intensely black).

For this reason some exegetes said regarding this verse that it is an instance of inversion (*al-muqaddam wa'l-mu'akhkhar*) in God's saying ﴿and intensely black (*ghara-ibu sud*)﴾, meaning *sud gharabib* (black, intensely so). But what they said is open to scrutiny.

Ibn Kathir (may Allah have mercy on him) says: Allah the Exalted informs about His servants, the believers, who recite His Book, believe in it, and act upon what is in it, by establishing the prayer and spending from what Allah has provided them, at the prescribed times, by night and by day, secretly and openly. ﴿They hope for a trade that will never perish﴾, meaning: they hope for a reward with Allah that is certain to be attained. As we mentioned at the beginning of the tafsir, in the section on the virtues of the Qur'an, it is said that it (the Qur'an) will say to its companion: "Every trader is behind his trade, and you are today behind every trade." Therefore Allah the Exalted said: ﴿so that He may pay them their rewards in full and increase them from His bounty﴾, meaning: so that He may pay them the reward for what they did and multiply it for them with increases that did not occur to them. ﴿Indeed He is Forgiving﴾, meaning: of their sins, ﴿Appreciative﴾, meaning: of the little of their deeds.

[Al-Musnad (3/38). Darraj has munkar narrations, and his narration from Abu al-Haytham is weak.] Very strange (gharib jiddan).

[Al-Musnad (3/38). Darraj has munkar narrations, and his narration from Abu al-Haytham is weak.] Very strange (gharib jiddan).

And that which We have revealed to you, O Muhammad, of the Book, which is the Qur'an, is the truth, confirming what was before it [[In T, S, A: "as it testified for it" (shahidat hiya)]] of the earlier scriptures; it confirms them, just as they testified to its [[In T, A: "prophethood" instead of "elevation"]] elevated status and that it is sent down from the Lord of the worlds.

Indeed, Allah is, with respect to His servants, All-Aware, All-Seeing. That is, He is Knowing of them and Seeing of who deserves what He favours him with over others. For this reason He preferred the prophets and messengers over all of mankind, preferred some of the prophets over others, raised some of them in rank by degrees, and placed the station of Muhammad ﷺ above all of them, may the blessings of Allah be upon them all.

Allah the Exalted says: Then We made those who inherit the Great Book, which confirms what came before it of the Books, the ones We chose from among Our servants. They are this Ummah. Then He divided them into three types [[In T: "categories".]], saying: ﴿Then among them is one who wrongs himself﴾. This is the one who neglects some of the obligatory duties and commits some of the prohibited acts. ﴿And among them is one who is moderate﴾. This is the one who performs the obligatory duties and abstains from the prohibited acts, though he may leave some of the recommended acts and do some of the disliked acts. ﴿And among them is one who is foremost in good deeds, by Allah's permission﴾. This is the one who performs the obligatory and recommended acts and abstains from the prohibited acts, the disliked acts, and some of the permissible acts.

ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭalḥah related from Ibn ʿAbbās regarding His saying: ﴿Then We caused to inherit the Book those whom We chose from among Our servants﴾ [[Added from T and S.]]. He said: They are the Ummah of Muhammad ﷺ. Allah made them inherit every Book He sent down. Their one who wrongs himself will be forgiven, their moderate one will be held to a light account, and their foremost one will enter Paradise without any reckoning.

Abu al-Qasim al-Tabarani said: Yahya ibn ʿUthman ibn Salih and ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn Muʿawiyah al-ʿUtbi narrated to us, both saying: Abu al-Tahir ibn al-Sarh narrated to us, Musa ibn ʿAbd al-Rahman al-San'ani narrated to us, Ibn Juraij narrated to me, from ʿAta', from Ibn ʿAbbas, from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, that he said one day: "My intercession is for the people of major sins from among my Ummah." Ibn ʿAbbas said: The foremost in good deeds will enter Paradise without reckoning, the moderate one will enter Paradise by the mercy of Allah, and the one who wrongs himself and the people of the Heights will enter Paradise by the intercession of Muhammad ﷺ. [[Al-Mu'jam al-Kabir (11/189). Ibn Jarir is a mudallis and has narrated here with ʿan'anah (without stating hearing).]]

Similarly, it has been related from more than one of the early predecessors (al-salaf) that the one who wrongs himself from this Ummah is among those chosen, despite the crookedness and shortcoming in him.

Others said: Rather, the one who wrongs himself is not from this Ummah, nor from the chosen ones who inherit the Book.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father narrated to us, ʿAli ibn Hashim ibn Marzuq narrated to us, Ibn ʿUyaynah narrated to us, from ʿAmr, from Ibn ʿAbbas, may Allah be pleased with them both [[In T: "He narrated from him."]]: ﴿Then among them is one who wrongs himself﴾. He said: He is the disbeliever. ʿIkrimah also narrated the same from him, and ʿIkrimah also said this, as narrated by Ibn Jarir.

Ibn Abi Najih said, from Mujahid, regarding His saying: ﴿Then among them is one who wrongs himself﴾: They are the companions of the left [[Ashab al-mash'amah.]].

Malik said, from Zayd ibn Aslam, al-Hasan, and Qatadah: He is the hypocrite.

Then Ibn ʿAbbas, al-Hasan, and Qatadah said: These three categories are like the three categories mentioned at the beginning and end of Surat al-Waqiʿah.

The correct view is that the one who wrongs himself is from this Ummah. This is the view chosen by Ibn Jarir, and it is the apparent meaning of the verse, and it is what the hadiths from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ have brought, through chains that strengthen one another. We will cite some of them, as much as is feasible:

The first hadith: Imam Ahmad said: Muhammad ibn Jaʿfar narrated to us, Shuʿbah narrated to us, from al-Walid ibn al-ʿAyzar, that he heard a man from Thaqif narrating from a man from Kinanah, from Abu Saʿid al-Khudri, may Allah be pleased with him, from the Prophet ﷺ, that he said concerning this verse: ﴿Then We caused to inherit the Book those whom We chose from among Our servants; then among them is one who wrongs himself, and among them is one who is moderate, and among them is one who is foremost in good deeds, by Allah's permission﴾, he said: "They are all of one rank and they are all in Paradise." This is a gharib (single-line) hadith from this route, and its chain includes an unnamed narrator. It has been narrated by Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim from the hadith of Shuʿbah, similarly. [[Al-Musnad (3/78) and Tafsir al-Tabari (22/90).]]

The meaning of his saying "of one rank" is: in that they are all from this Ummah and all of them are among the people of Paradise, even though there are differences in their ranks in Paradise.

The second hadith: Imam Ahmad said: Ishaq ibn ʿIsa narrated to us, Anas ibn ʿIyad al-Laythi Abu Damrah narrated to us, from Musa ibn ʿUqbah, from ʿAli [[Added from S and A.]] ibn ʿAbd Allah al-Azdi, from Abu al-Darda', [[In T: "Imam Ahmad narrated with his chain from Abu al-Darda'."]] may Allah be pleased with him, who said: I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: "Allah said: ﴿Then We caused to inherit the Book those whom We chose from among Our servants; then among them is one who wrongs himself, and among them is one who is moderate, and among them is one who is foremost in good deeds, by Allah's permission﴾. As for those who were foremost, they are the ones who will enter Paradise without reckoning. As for those who were moderate, they will be held to a light reckoning. As for those who wronged themselves, they are the ones who will be detained for a long time on the Gathering Place. Then they are the ones whom Allah will overtake with His mercy, and they are the ones who will say: ﴿All praise is due to Allah, who has removed from us the grief. Indeed, our Lord is Forgiving and Appreciative. Who has settled us in the home of settlement by His bounty; no fatigue touches us therein, nor does weariness touch us therein﴾." [[Al-Musnad (5/198).]]

Another route: [[In T: "It was also narrated through another route."]] Ibn Abi Hatim said: Usayd ibn ʿAsim narrated to us, al-Husayn ibn Hafs narrated to us, Sufyan narrated to us, from al-Aʿmash, from a man, from Abu Thabit, from Abu al-Darda', who said: I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: ﴿Then We caused to inherit the Book those whom We chose from among Our servants; then among them is one who wrongs himself﴾, and he said: "As for the one who wrongs himself, he will be detained until distress and sorrow befall him, and then he will enter Paradise."

Ibn Jarir also narrated it from the hadith of Sufyan al-Thawri, from al-Aʿmash, who said: Abu Thabit mentioned that he entered the mosque and sat beside Abu al-Darda', and said: "O Allah, ease my loneliness, have mercy on my strangeness, and grant me a righteous companion." Abu al-Darda' said: "If you are truthful, then I am happier with you than you are with me. I will narrate to you a hadith that I heard from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, which I have not narrated since I heard it from him." He mentioned this verse: ﴿Then We caused to inherit the Book those whom We chose from among Our servants; then among them is one who wrongs himself, and among them is one who is moderate, and among them is one who is foremost in good deeds﴾, and said: "As for the one foremost in good deeds, he will enter it without reckoning. As for the moderate one, he will be held to a light reckoning. As for the one who wrongs himself, he will suffer in that place distress and sorrow, and that is His saying: ﴿All praise is due to Allah, who has removed from us the grief﴾." [[Tafsir al-Tabari (22/90). Al-Hakim narrated it in al-Mustadrak (2/426), and al-Bayhaqi in al-Ba'th (no. 62) by way of al-Aʿmash, with the same chain.]]

The third hadith: The Hafiz Abu al-Qasim al-Tabarani said: ʿAbd Allah ibn Muhammad ibn al-ʿAbbas narrated to us, Ibn Masʿud narrated to us, Sahl ibn ʿAbd Rabbihi [[In A: "ʿAbd Allah."]] al-Razzi informed us, ʿAmr ibn Abi Qays narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Layla, from his brother, from ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn Abi Layla [[In T: "The Hafiz Abu al-Qasim al-Tabarani narrated it with his chain."]], from Usamah ibn Zayd: ﴿Then among them is one who wrongs himself, and among them is one who is moderate, and among them is one who is foremost in good deeds﴾, the verse, and he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "All of them are from this Ummah." [[Al-Mu'jam al-Kabir (1/167). There is a break in its chain. Al-Bayhaqi narrated it in al-Ba'th (no. 64) by way of Muhammad ibn Saʿid, from ʿAmr ibn Abi Qays, from Ibn Abi Layla, from his brother ʿIsa, from his father, from Usamah ibn Zayd, with the same wording. He also narrated it (no. 63) by way of Husayn ibn Numayr, from Ibn Abi Layla, from his brother, from his father, from Usamah ibn Zayd, with similar wording.]]

The fourth hadith: Ibn Abi Hatim said: Muhammad ibn ʿAziz narrated to us, Salamah narrated to us, from ʿAqil, from Ibn Shihab, from ʿAwf [[In A: "Anas."]] ibn Malik, from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, that he said: "My Ummah is in three thirds: a third will enter Paradise without reckoning or punishment, a third will be held to a light reckoning and then enter Paradise, and a third will be purified and examined. Then the angels will come and say: 'We found them saying: "There is no god but Allah alone."' Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, will say: 'They spoke the truth. There is no god but Me. Admit them into Paradise because of their saying: "There is no god but Allah alone." And place their sins upon the people of the Fire.' These are the sins that Allah the Exalted mentioned: ﴿And they will surely bear their burdens and burdens along with their burdens﴾ [al-ʿAnkabut: 13]. And its confirmation is in the verse that mentions the angels, where Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Then We caused to inherit the Book those whom We chose from among Our servants﴾, so He made them three types [[In T and S: "groups."]], and they are all categories. Among them is one who wrongs himself, and this is the one who will be examined and purified." Very gharib. [[Al-Tabarani narrated it in al-Mu'jam al-Kabir (18/80) by way of Muhammad ibn ʿAziz. Al-Haythami said in al-Majma' (7/96): "In its chain is Salamah ibn Rawh, whom Ibn Hibban declared trustworthy, while others weakened him; the rest of its narrators are trustworthy."]]

A report from Ibn Masʿud: Ibn Jarir said: Ibn Humayd narrated to me, al-Hakim ibn Bashir narrated to us, from ʿAmr ibn Qays, from ʿAbd Allah ibn ʿIsa, from Yazid ibn al-Harith, from Shaqiq Abu Wa'il, from ʿAbd Allah ibn Masʿud, that he said: This Ummah is three thirds on the Day of Resurrection: a third will enter Paradise without reckoning, a third will be held to a light reckoning, and a third will come with great sins, until He says: "What are these?"—and He knows best, may He be blessed and exalted. The angels will say: "These have come with great sins, except that they did not associate anything with You." The Lord, Mighty and Majestic, will say: "Admit these into the vastness of My mercy." Then ʿAbd Allah recited this verse: ﴿Then We caused to inherit the Book those whom We chose from among Our servants [so among them is one who wrongs himself]﴾ [[Added from A.]], the verse.

Another report: Abu Dawud al-Tayalisi said, from al-Salt ibn Dinar Abu Shuʿayb [[In H and S: "Dinar ibn al-Ash'ath," and in A: "from al-Ash'ath," the version here is from Musnad al-Tayalisi.]], from ʿUqbah ibn Suhban al-Hunaʾi, who said: I asked ʿAʾishah, may Allah be pleased with her, about the saying of Allah: ﴿Then We caused to inherit the Book those whom We chose from among Our servants; then among them is one who wrongs himself﴾, the verse. She said to me: "My son, these are in Paradise. As for the foremost in good deeds, they are those who passed away during the time of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, to whom the Messenger of Allah ﷺ bore witness of life and provision. As for the moderate, they are those who followed his way among his companions until they joined him. As for the one who wrongs himself, he is like me and like you." He said: So she placed herself with us. [[Musnad al-Tayalisi, no. 1489.]]

Have you not seen that Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Then We caused to inherit the Book those whom We chose from among Our servants. Among them is one who wrongs himself, and among them is one who is moderate, and among them is one who is foremost in good deeds by Allah's permission. That is the great bounty: Gardens of Eternity, which they will enter﴾ up to His saying: ﴿And as for those who disbelieve, for them is the Fire of Hell﴾." He said: "These are the people of the Fire."

Ibn Jarir narrated it through several chains from Awf, with the same wording. Then he said:

Ya'qub ibn Ibrahim narrated to me, saying: Ibn 'Ulayyah narrated to us, saying: Humayd informed us, from Ishaq ibn Abdullah ibn al-Harith, from his father, that Ibn 'Abbas asked Ka'b about His saying: ﴿Then We caused to inherit the Book those whom We chose from among Our servants﴾ up to His saying: ﴿by Allah's permission﴾. He said: "Their shoulders touched, and by the Lord of Ka'b [in another version: "the Ka'bah"], then they were given the bounty according to their deeds."

Then Ibn Jarir said: Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: al-Hakam ibn Bashir narrated to us, saying: Amr ibn Qays narrated to us, from Abu Ishaq al-Sabi'i concerning this verse: ﴿Then We caused to inherit the Book those whom We chose from among Our servants﴾ the verse. Then he said: Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: al-Hakam narrated to us, saying: Amr narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn al-Hanafiyyah, who said: "Indeed, this is a merciful Ummah: the one who wrongs himself is forgiven, the moderate one is in the Gardens with Allah, and the foremost in good deeds is in the high ranks with Allah."

It was also narrated by al-Thawri, from Isma'il ibn Sami', from a man, from Muhammad ibn al-Hanafiyyah, with similar meaning.

Abu al-Jarud said: I asked Muhammad ibn Ali (i.e., al-Baqir) about His saying: ﴿Among them is one who wrongs himself﴾, and he said: "He is the one who mixed a righteous deed with another evil one."

This is what was readily available of the narrations and reports related to this station. Having established this, the verse is general in all three categories of this Ummah. The scholars are the most envied of people for this blessing and the most deserving of people for this mercy. As Imam Ahmad, may Allah have mercy on him, said:

Muhammad ibn Yazid narrated to us, saying: Asim ibn Raja' ibn Haywah narrated to us, from Qays ibn Kathir, who said: A man from the people of Madinah came to Abu al-Darda', while he was in Damascus, and said: "What brought you, my brother?" He said: "A hadith that reached me that you narrate from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ." He said: "Did you not come for trade?" He said: "No." He said: "Did you not come for some need?" He said: "No." He said: "Did you come for nothing but this hadith?" He said: "Yes." He said: "Indeed I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: 'Whoever takes a path seeking knowledge therein, Allah will make a path to Paradise easy for him by it. Indeed the angels lower their wings out of pleasure for the seeker of knowledge. Indeed the one who has knowledge is asked forgiveness by whoever is in the heavens and the earth, even the fish in the water. The superiority of the scholar over the worshipper is like the superiority of the moon over the rest of the stars. Indeed the scholars are the heirs of the Prophets, and indeed the Prophets did not bequeath dinar or dirham; they bequeathed only knowledge, so whoever takes it has taken a abundant portion.'"

Abu Dawud, al-Tirmidhi and Ibn Majah also narrated it, from the hadith of Kathir ibn Qays (and some say Qays ibn Kathir), from Abu al-Darda'. We have mentioned its chains and the differences among its narrators in the explanation of the "Book of Knowledge" in Sahih al-Bukhari, and to Allah belongs all praise and grace.

It has already preceded at the beginning of Surah Ta-Ha the hadith of Tha'labah ibn al-Hakam, from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, who said: "Allah the Exalted says on the Day of Resurrection to the scholars: 'I did not place My knowledge and My judgment among you except that I intended to forgive you for what was from you, and I do not mind.'" [The takhrij of this hadith was mentioned at the commentary of verse (2) of Surah Ta-Ha.]

This is as established in the Sahih (authentic collection) from Abu Hurairah, may Allah be pleased with him, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "The adornment will reach the believer wherever the ablution water reaches." [Abu Nu'aym narrated it in Sifat al-Jannah, no. (267), through 'Ali ibn al-Hasan, from Amr ibn Sawad, with the same chain. Al-Hasan al-Basri did not hear from Abu Hurairah.]

﴿And they will say: "All praise is for Allah, who has removed from us grief"﴾. Grief is fear of what is to be dreaded. He removed it from us and relieved us of what we used to fear and beware of, from the worries of this world and the Hereafter.

Al-Tabarani said: Ja'far ibn Muhammad al-Firyabi narrated to us, Yahya ibn Musa al-Marwazi narrated to us, Sulayman ibn Abd Allah ibn Wahb al-Kufi narrated to us, from Abd al-Aziz ibn Hakim, from Ibn Umar, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "There is no loneliness for the people of "La ilaha illa Allah" at death, nor in their graves, nor at the resurrection. (88), narrated it through al-Hasan, from Bahlul ibn Ubayd, from Salamah ibn Kuhayl, from Ibn Umar, in similar wording. al-Bayhaqi said: "This is mursal from Salamah ibn Kuhayl and Ibn Umar; Bahlul is alone in it and is not strong."]

Ibn Abbas and others said: He forgave them much of their misdeeds and appreciated from them the little of good deeds.

﴿He who has settled us in the abode of permanence from His bounty﴾. They say: He who gave us this station and this position out of His bounty, grace and mercy; our deeds did not equal that. * *

As for His saying: ﴿And they will cry out therein﴾, that is: they will call out therein, crying out to Allah, exalted and majestic is He, with their voices: ﴿Our Lord, bring us out; we will do righteousness, other than what we used to do.﴾ That is, they ask to be returned to the world so that they may do other than their former deeds. The Lord, majestic in His majesty, knows that if He returned them to the worldly abode, they would revert to what they had been forbidden, and indeed they are liars. Therefore He does not answer their request, as Allah, exalted is He, related about them in their saying: ﴿Is there any way out? That is because, when Allah was called upon alone, you disbelieved, and when partners were associated with Him, you believed.﴾ [Ghafir: 11-12] That is: He does not respond to you in this, because you were like that, and if you were returned you would return to what you were forbidden. Therefore He said here: ﴿Did We not give you life long enough that whoever would be mindful could be mindful therein?﴾ That is: did you not live in the world for lifespans in which, if you had been among those who benefit from the truth, you would have benefited from it during the span of your life?

The exegetes have differed regarding the length of life meant here. It is narrated from ʿAli ibn al-Husayn Zayn al-ʿAbidin that he said: it is the length of seventeen years.

Qatadah said: Know that a long life is a proof (against a person), so we seek refuge in Allah from being deceived by a long life. This verse was revealed, ﴿Did We not give you life long enough that whoever would be mindful could be mindful therein?﴾, and among them was a youth of eighteen years. Abu Ghalib al-Shaybani also said likewise.

ʿAbdullah ibn al-Mubarak said, from Maʿmar, from a man, from Wahb ibn Munabbih, regarding His saying: ﴿Did We not give you life long enough that whoever would be mindful could be mindful therein?﴾ that he said: twenty years.

Hushaym said, from Mansur, from Zadhan, from al-Hasan regarding His saying: ﴿Did We not give you life long enough that whoever would be mindful could be mindful therein?﴾ that he said: forty years.

Hushaym also said, from Mujahid, from al-Shaʿbi, from Masruq, that he used to say: when one of you reaches forty years, let him take his caution from Allah, mighty and majestic is He.

And this is a narration from Ibn ʿAbbas, as Ibn Jarir said: Ibn ʿAbd al-Aʿla narrated to us, Bishr ibn al-Mufaddal narrated to us, ʿAbdullah ibn ʿUthman ibn Khuthaym narrated to us, from Mujahid who said: I heard Ibn ʿAbbas say: The lifespan through which Allah established His proof against the son of Adam is: ﴿Did We not give you life long enough that whoever would be mindful could be mindful therein?﴾ forty years.

Thus he narrated it from this route, from Ibn ʿAbbas. This view is the choice of Ibn Jarir. Then he narrated it from the route of al-Thawri and ʿAbdullah ibn Idris, both from ʿAbdullah ibn ʿUthman ibn Khuthaym, from Mujahid [in another narration], from Ibn ʿAbbas who said: The lifespan through which Allah established His proof against the son of Adam, in His saying: ﴿Did We not give you life long enough that whoever would be mindful could be mindful therein?﴾ is sixty years.

This narration is more authentic from Ibn ʿAbbas, and it is also the correct one in reality, due to what is established in the hadith on this matter, as we will cite, not as Ibn Jarir claimed, that the hadith is not authentic because its chain includes someone whose reliability must be verified.

Abu Nubat, from ʿAli, may Allah be pleased with him, related that he said: The lifespan by which Allah reproached them in His saying, ﴿Did We not give you life long enough that whoever would be mindful could be mindful therein?﴾, is sixty years.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father narrated to us, Duhaym narrated to us, Ibn Abi Fudayk narrated to us, Ibrahim ibn al-Fadl al-Makhzumi narrated to me, from Ibn Abi Husayn al-Makki, that ʿAta (that is, Ibn Abi Rabah) narrated to him from Ibn ʿAbbas, may Allah be pleased with both of them [in another, "from him"], that the Prophet ﷺ said: "When the Day of Resurrection comes, it will be said: Where are the people of sixty years? And that is the lifespan of which Allah said: ﴿Did We not give you life long enough that whoever would be mindful could be mindful therein, and the warner came to you?﴾"

Ibn Jarir also narrated it similarly, from ʿAli ibn Shuʿayb, from Muhammad ibn Ismaʿil [in all copies: "from Ismaʿil," and the correct form is from Al-Tabari] ibn Abi Fudayk, with the same chain. Al-Tabarani also narrated it from the route of Ibn Abi Fudayk, with the same chain. This hadith is problematic because of the condition of Ibrahim ibn al-Fadl, and Allah knows best.

Allah, the Exalted, informs of His knowledge of the unseen of the heavens and the earth, and that He knows what the hidden secrets conceal and what the inner thoughts harbor, and that He will recompense every doer for his deed.

Then He said: ﴿It is He who made you successors upon the earth﴾, meaning: one people succeeds another before them, and one generation succeeds the generation before them, as He said: ﴿and makes you successors of the earth﴾ [An-Naml: 62]. ﴿Whoever disbelieves, upon him is his disbelief﴾, meaning: the burden of that falls only upon himself and not upon anyone else. ﴿And the disbelief of the disbelievers does not increase them, in the sight of their Lord, except in abhorrence﴾, meaning: whenever they persist in their disbelief, Allah hates them, and whenever they persist in it, they lose themselves and their families on the Day of Resurrection. In contrast to the believers, whenever one of them lives longer and his deeds are good, his rank and station in Paradise are raised, his reward increases, and his Creator and Originator, the Lord of the worlds, loves him. [Exalted is the Decreer, the Arranger, the Lord of the worlds.]

He, exalted is He, tells His Messenger ﷺ to say to the polytheists: ﴿Have you considered your partners whom you invoke besides Allah?﴾ That is, the idols and rivals. ﴿Show me what they have created from the earth, or do they have a share in the heavens?﴾ That is, they have no share in any of that, and they do not possess even a qitmir (the thin membrane of a date-stone).

* *

And His saying: ﴿Or have We given them a Book so that they are upon clear proof from it?﴾ That is, have We sent down to them a Book that supports what they say of shirk and disbelief? The matter is not so. ﴿Rather, the wrongdoers promise one another nothing but delusion.﴾ That is, they only followed in this their desires, their opinions, and their wishful thinking which they imagined for themselves, and these are delusion, falsehood, and lies.

Then He, exalted is He, informed of His great power by which the heavens and the earth stand by His command, and of the force placed in them that holds them, saying: ﴿Indeed, Allah holds the heavens and the earth lest they cease.﴾ That is, lest they shake from their places. As He said: ﴿And He holds back the sky from falling upon the earth except by His permission﴾ [al-Hajj: 65], and He, exalted is He, said: ﴿And among His signs is that the sky and the earth stand by His command﴾ [al-Rum: 25]. ﴿And if they should cease, none could hold them after Him.﴾ That is, none is able to sustain them and keep them in existence except Him. And He, with all that, is Forbearing (ḥalīm), Oft-Forgiving (ghafūr). That is, He sees His servants disbelieving in Him and disobeying Him, yet He is forbearing toward them, so He delays, gives respite, postpones, and does not hasten; He covers over others and forgives. Therefore He said: ﴿Indeed, He is ever Forbearing, Oft-Forgiving.﴾

Ibn Abi Hatim has cited here a hadith that is gharib (singular), indeed munkar (rejected). He said: "Ali ibn al-Husayn ibn al-Junayd narrated to us, Ishaq ibn Ibrahim narrated to us, Hisham ibn Yusuf narrated to me, from Umayyah ibn Shibl, from al-Hakam ibn Aban, from Ikrimah, from [in T: 'with its chain to Abu Hurayrah'] Abu Hurayrah who said: I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ relating from Musa (peace be upon him) on the pulpit, he said: 'It occurred to Musa (peace be upon him) in his heart: Does Allah, Mighty and Majestic, sleep? So Allah sent to him an angel, who kept him awake for three nights, and gave him two flasks, one in each hand, and ordered him to guard them. He said: So he began to sleep, and his hands were almost meeting, then he would awaken and hold one of them back from the other, until he slept his sleep, and his hands jerked and the two flasks broke. He said: Allah struck for him a parable: that if Allah were to sleep, the heavens and the earth would not remain firm.'"

The apparent meaning is that this hadith is not marfu' (traced to the Prophet ﷺ), but rather from the rejected Israiliyyat (narratives of Israelite origin). Musa (peace be upon him) is far too exalted to attribute sleep to Allah, glorified and exalted is He, and Allah has informed in His Mighty Book that He is: ﴿The Ever-Living, the Sustainer of all existence. Neither drowsiness nor sleep overtakes Him. To Him belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth﴾ [al-Baqarah: 255]. And it is established in the two Sahihs (Sahih al-Bukhari and Sahih Muslim) from Abu Musa al-Ash'ari, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Indeed Allah does not sleep, nor does it befit Him to sleep. He lowers the scale and raises it. The deeds of the night are raised to Him before the deeds of the day, and the deeds of the day before the night. His veil is light, or fire; were He to remove it, the splendors of His face would burn away whatever of His creation His sight reaches."

[Footnote: Sahih Muslim, no. (179), and it is not in Sahih al-Bukhari; the Hafiz (Ibn Hajar) mentioned it at the commentary on verse 255 of Surah al-Baqarah saying: "In the Sahih thus, in the singular."]

Abu Ja'far ibn Jarir (al-Tabari) said: Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, Sufyan narrated to us, from al-A'mash, from Abu Wa'il who said: A man came to Abdullah (he is Ibn Mas'ud) and said: "From where have you come?" He said: "From al-Sham." He said: "Whom did you meet?" He said: "I met Ka'b." He said: "What did Ka'b narrate to you?" He said: "He told me that the heavens revolve upon the shoulder of an angel." He said: "Did you believe him or did you deny him?" He said: "I neither believed him nor denied him." He said: "I wish you had ransomed your journey to him with your mount and its saddle. Ka'b lied. Indeed Allah, exalted is He, says: ﴿Indeed, Allah holds the heavens and the earth lest they cease, and if they should cease, none could hold them after Him.﴾"

[Footnote: Tafsir al-Tabari (22/94).]

This chain is sahih up to Ka'b and up to Ibn Mas'ud. Then al-Tabari narrated it from Ibn Humayd, from Jarir, from Mughirah, from Ibrahim who said: Jundub al-Bajali went to Ka'b in al-Sham, and he mentioned something similar.

[Footnote: Tafsir al-Tabari (22/95).] I have seen in the Musannaf of the jurist Yahya ibn Ibrahim ibn Muzayn al-Tulaytuli, which he named "Sir al-Fuqaha" (The Biography of the Jurists), that he cited this report from Muhammad ibn Isa ibn al-Tabba', from Waki', from al-A'mash, with it. Then he said: Zuwan informed us, meaning Abd al-Malik ibn al-Hasan, from Ibn Wahb, from Malik that he said: "The sky does not revolve," and he cited this verse as evidence, and the hadith: "Indeed, in the west there is a door of repentance that remains open until the sun rises from it."

I say: this hadith is in the Sahih [Footnote: I did not find the hadith in the two Sahihs; it is in Sunan al-Tirmidhi, no. (3536), Sahih Ibn Khuzaymah, no. (193), and the Musnad of Imam Ahmad (4/240), with a matching hadith from Safwan ibn Assal, may Allah be pleased with him, and its wording in Ibn Khuzaymah is: "Indeed, in the west there is a door open for repentance, its width is seventy years' journey, it will not be closed until the sun rises from its west," similar.], and Allah knows best.

Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Qur'an al-'Azim) on Surah 35, verses 42–43:

Allah, the Exalted, informs us that the Quraysh and the Arabs swore by Allah with their most emphatic oaths, before the Messenger was sent to them: "If a warner came to us, we would surely be better guided than any (one of) the (other) nations." That is, better guided than all the nations to which messengers were sent. This was said by al-Dahhak and others, like the verse: "Lest you should say, 'The Scripture was only sent down upon two groups before us, and we were indeed unaware of their study.' Or lest you should say, 'If the Scripture had been revealed to us, we would have been better guided than them.' But there has come to you clear evidence from your Lord, and guidance and mercy. So who is more unjust than one who denies the verses of Allah and turns away from them?" [al-An'am: 156–157] [[In manuscript T: "or they say."]] And like His saying: "And indeed they used to say, 'If we had a reminder from the former peoples, we would have been sincere servants of Allah.' But they disbelieved in it, so they are going to know." [al-Saffat: 167–170]

Allah said: "But when a warner came to them" — and he is Muhammad (ﷺ) — "with what was revealed with him of the Great Scripture, which is the manifest Qur'an, it increased them only in aversion." That is, it only increased them in disbelief added to their disbelief. Then He explained this with His saying: "in arrogance upon the earth and plotting of evil." That is, they were arrogant against following the signs of Allah. "And the evil plotting" means they plotted against the people in turning them away from the path of Allah. "But the evil plotting does not beset anyone except its own people." That is, the consequence of that plotting returns only upon them, themselves, and no one else.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: 'Ali ibn al-Husayn mentioned to us, Ibn Abi 'Umar narrated to us, Sufyan narrated to us, from Abu Zakariyya al-Kufi, from a man who narrated to him, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Beware of evil plotting, for evil plotting does not beset anyone except its own people, and for them is a seeker from Allah." [[This is mursal, and I have not found anyone who transmitted it other than Ibn Abi Hatim. Ibn al-Mubarak in al-Zuhd (no. 725) narrated something similar from al-Zuhri as a mursal report.]] Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi also said: "Three things, whoever does them will not be safe until it befalls him: plotting, transgression, or breaking a covenant. Their confirmation is in the Book of Allah: 'But evil plotting does not beset anyone except its own people' [Fatir 43]; 'Your transgression is only against yourselves' [Yunus 23]; 'Whoever breaks his oath, only breaks it to his own detriment' [al-Fath 10]."

And His saying: "So do they await except the way of the former peoples?" That means the punishment of Allah upon them for their denial of His messengers and their opposition to His command. "But you will not find any change in the way of Allah, and you will not find any alteration in the way of Allah." That is, it is not altered or changed, but rather it continues in this manner against every denier. "And you will not find any diversion in the way of Allah" — that is, "And when Allah intends harm for a people, there is no repelling it" [al-Ra'd 11], and no one can lift that from them or divert it away from them.

Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 35, verses 44–45:

He, exalted is He, says: Say, O Muhammad, to these deniers of what you have brought them of the message: "Travel through the earth and see what was the end of those who denied the messengers." How God destroyed them, and there are similar fates for the disbelievers. Their dwellings became empty of them, and they were stripped of the blessings they had enjoyed after their full strength, their great numbers and equipment, and their abundant wealth and children. So none of that availed them anything, and it did not repel from them any of God's punishment when the command of your Lord came, because He, exalted is He, is not incapable of anything whenever He wills it, whether in the heavens or on the earth. ﴿Indeed, He is ever Knowing, Competent.﴾ That is, He knows all existing things and is capable of all of them together.

Then He, exalted is He, said: ﴿And if God were to seize mankind for what they have earned, He would not leave upon the earth [any] creature.﴾ That is, if He were to seize them for all their sins, He would destroy all the people of the earth and all the creatures and provisions they possess.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Ahmad ibn Sinan narrated to us, 'Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, Sufyan al-Thawri narrated to us, from Abu Ishaq, from Abu al-Ahwas, from 'Abdullah [ibn Mas'ud], who said: "The dung beetle nearly gets punished in its hole because of the sin of the son of Adam." Then he recited: ﴿And if God were to seize mankind for what they have earned, He would not leave upon its back [any] creature.﴾

Sa'id ibn Jubayr and al-Suddi said, regarding His words ﴿He would not leave upon its back [any] creature﴾: that is, if He were to withhold the rain from them, all the creatures would die.

﴿But He defers them to a specified term.﴾ That is, He gives them respite until the Day of Resurrection, when He will call them to account and will repay every doer for his deed, rewarding with reward those who obey and with punishment those who disobey. Therefore He, exalted is He, said: ﴿So when their term comes, indeed God is ever Seeing of His servants.﴾

This is the end of the tafsir of Surah Fatir, and praise and grace belong to God.

Tafsir of Surah Ya-Sin.

It is Meccan.

Abu 'Isa al-Tirmidhi said: Qutaybah and Sufyan ibn Wakee' narrated to us, Humayd ibn 'Abd al-Rahman al-Ru'asi narrated to us, from al-Hasan ibn Salih, from Harun Abu Muhammad, from Muqatil ibn Hayyan, from Qatadah, from Anas, who said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "Indeed, everything has a heart, and the heart of the Qur'an is Ya-Sin. Whoever recites Ya-Sin, God records for him, for its recitation, the reward of reciting the Qur'an ten times."

Then he said: This is a strange hadith, which we know only through the narration of Humayd ibn 'Abd al-Rahman. Harun Abu Muhammad is an unknown shaykh. On this subject there is also [a report] from Abu Bakr al-Siddiq, may God be pleased with him, but it is not sound because of the weakness of its isnad, and from Abu Hurayrah, which is open to scrutiny.

[Footnote: Sunan al-Tirmidhi, no. (2887). Ibn Abi Hatim said in al-'Ilal (2/56), after mentioning the hadith: "My father said: Muqatil here is Muqatil ibn Sulayman. I saw this hadith at the beginning of a book composed by Muqatil, and it is a false hadith with no basis. I asked my father: Did Muqatil meet Qatadah? He said: And Abu al-Zubayr is older than Qatadah."]

As for the hadith of al-Siddiq, al-Hakim al-Tirmidhi narrated it in his book Nawadir al-Usul. [Footnote: Nawadir al-Usul, p. (335). It was also narrated by Ibn al-Daris in Fada'il al-Qur'an, no. (217), al-Bayhaqi in Shu'ab al-Iman, no. (2465), and Ibn al-Jawzi in al-Mawdu'at (1/247), through several chains from Isma'il ibn Abi Uways, from Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-Rahman al-Ju'dani, from Sulayman ibn Mirqa', from Hilal ibn al-Salt, from Abu Bakr, may God be pleased with him. Ibn al-Jawzi said: "This hadith, in all its chains, is false and has no basis."]

As for the hadith of Abu Hurayrah, Abu Bakr al-Bazzar said: 'Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Fadl narrated to us, Zayd, that is Ibn al-Hubab, narrated to us, Humayd, that is al-Makki, client of the family of 'Alqamah, narrated to us, from 'Ata', that is Ibn Abi Rabah, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "Indeed, everything has a heart, and the heart of the Qur'an is Ya-Sin."

Then he said: We know of no one who narrated this except Zayd, from Humayd. [Footnote: Musnad al-Bazzar, no. (2304), "Kashf al-Astar."]

The hafiz Abu Ya'la said: Ishaq ibn Abi Isra'il narrated to us, Hajjaj ibn Muhammad narrated to us, from Hisham ibn Ziyad, from al-Hasan, who said: I heard Abu Hurayrah say: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "Whoever recites Ya-Sin on a night will wake in the morning forgiven. And whoever recites Ha-Mim, the one in which there is smoke [Surah al-Dukhan], will wake in the morning forgiven." Its isnad is good. [Footnote: Musnad Abi Ya'la (11/93). In its isnad is Hisham ibn Ziyad, whom the imams declared weak. Ibn Hibban said: "He was among those who narrated fabrications from trustworthy narrators and reversed reports from reliable narrators, so that it comes to the mind of the listener that he was the one relied upon for them, and it is not permissible to argue with him." Al-Hasan did not hear from Abu Hurayrah; see the note on Abu Ya'la at his words "I heard."]

Ibn Hibban said in his Sahih: Muhammad ibn Ishaq ibn Ibrahim, client of Thaqif, narrated to us, al-Walid ibn Shuja' ibn al-Walid al-Sakuni narrated to us, my father narrated to us, Ziyad ibn Khaytamah narrated to us, Muhammad ibn Juhadah narrated to us, from al-Hasan, from Jundab ibn 'Abdullah, who said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "Whoever recites Ya-Sin on a night seeking the face of God, he will be forgiven." [Footnote: Sahih Ibn Hibban, no. (665), "Mawarid." Al-Hasan did not hear from Jundab, according to Abu Hatim.]

Imam Ahmad has also said: 'Arim narrated to us, Mu'tamir narrated to us, from his father, from a man, from his father, from Ma'qil ibn Yasar, may God be pleased with him, that the Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "al-Baqarah is the hump and peak of the Qur'an. With each of its verses, eighty angels descended. And [the verse] ﴿God, there is no deity except Him, the Living, the Sustainer﴾ [al-Baqarah 2:255] was brought out from beneath the Throne and joined to it, or: it was joined to Surah al-Baqarah. And Ya-Sin is the heart of the Qur'an. No man recites it seeking God and the Hereafter except that he is forgiven. And recite it over your dead."

Al-Nasa'i narrated it in al-Yawm wa al-Layla in the same way, from Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-A'la, from Mu'tamir ibn Sulayman, with it. [Footnote: Al-Musnad (5/26); al-Nasa'i, al-Sunan al-Kubra, no. Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 35, verses 44–45:

He, exalted is He, says: Say, O Muhammad, to these deniers of what you have brought them of the message: "Travel through the earth and see what was the end of those who denied the messengers." How God destroyed them, and there are similar fates for the disbelievers. Their dwellings became empty of them, and they were stripped of the blessings they had enjoyed after their full strength, their great numbers and equipment, and their abundant wealth and children. So none of that availed them anything, and it did not repel from them any of God's punishment when the command of your Lord came, because He, exalted is He, is not incapable of anything whenever He wills it, whether in the heavens or on the earth. ﴿Indeed, He is ever Knowing, Competent.﴾ That is, He knows all existing things and is capable of all of them together.

Then He, exalted is He, said: ﴿And if God were to seize mankind for what they have earned, He would not leave upon the earth [any] creature.﴾ That is, if He were to seize them for all their sins, He would destroy all the people of the earth and all the creatures and provisions they possess.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Ahmad ibn Sinan narrated to us, 'Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, Sufyan al-Thawri narrated to us, from Abu Ishaq, from Abu al-Ahwas, from 'Abdullah [ibn Mas'ud], who said: "The dung beetle nearly gets punished in its hole because of the sin of the son of Adam." Then he recited: ﴿And if God were to seize mankind for what they have earned, He would not leave upon its back [any] creature.﴾

Sa'id ibn Jubayr and al-Suddi said, regarding His words ﴿He would not leave upon its back [any] creature﴾: that is, if He were to withhold the rain from them, all the creatures would die.

﴿But He defers them to a specified term.﴾ That is, He gives them respite until the Day of Resurrection, when He will call them to account and will repay every doer for his deed, rewarding with reward those who obey and with punishment those who disobey. Therefore He, exalted is He, said: ﴿So when their term comes, indeed God is ever Seeing of His servants.﴾

This is the end of the tafsir of Surah Fatir, and praise and grace belong to God.

Tafsir of Surah Ya-Sin.

It is Meccan.

Abu 'Isa al-Tirmidhi said: Qutaybah and Sufyan ibn Wakee' narrated to us, Humayd ibn 'Abd al-Rahman al-Ru'asi narrated to us, from al-Hasan ibn Salih, from Harun Abu Muhammad, from Muqatil ibn Hayyan, from Qatadah, from Anas, who said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "Indeed, everything has a heart, and the heart of the Qur'an is Ya-Sin. Whoever recites Ya-Sin, God records for him, for its recitation, the reward of reciting the Qur'an ten times."

Then he said: This is a strange hadith, which we know only through the narration of Humayd ibn 'Abd al-Rahman. Harun Abu Muhammad is an unknown shaykh. On this subject there is also [a report] from Abu Bakr al-Siddiq, may God be pleased with him, but it is not sound because of the weakness of its isnad, and from Abu Hurayrah, which is open to scrutiny.

[Footnote: Sunan al-Tirmidhi, no. (2887). Ibn Abi Hatim said in al-'Ilal (2/56), after mentioning the hadith: "My father said: Muqatil here is Muqatil ibn Sulayman. I saw this hadith at the beginning of a book composed by Muqatil, and it is a false hadith with no basis. I asked my father: Did Muqatil meet Qatadah? He said: And Abu al-Zubayr is older than Qatadah."]

As for the hadith of al-Siddiq, al-Hakim al-Tirmidhi narrated it in his book Nawadir al-Usul. [Footnote: Nawadir al-Usul, p. (335). It was also narrated by Ibn al-Daris in Fada'il al-Qur'an, no. (217), al-Bayhaqi in Shu'ab al-Iman, no. (2465), and Ibn al-Jawzi in al-Mawdu'at (1/247), through several chains from Isma'il ibn Abi Uways, from Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-Rahman al-Ju'dani, from Sulayman ibn Mirqa', from Hilal ibn al-Salt, from Abu Bakr, may God be pleased with him. Ibn al-Jawzi said: "This hadith, in all its chains, is false and has no basis."]

As for the hadith of Abu Hurayrah, Abu Bakr al-Bazzar said: 'Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Fadl narrated to us, Zayd, that is Ibn al-Hubab, narrated to us, Humayd, that is al-Makki, client of the family of 'Alqamah, narrated to us, from 'Ata', that is Ibn Abi Rabah, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "Indeed, everything has a heart, and the heart of the Qur'an is Ya-Sin."

Then he said: We know of no one who narrated this except Zayd, from Humayd. [Footnote: Musnad al-Bazzar, no. (2304), "Kashf al-Astar."]

The hafiz Abu Ya'la said: Ishaq ibn Abi Isra'il narrated to us, Hajjaj ibn Muhammad narrated to us, from Hisham ibn Ziyad, from al-Hasan, who said: I heard Abu Hurayrah say: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "Whoever recites Ya-Sin on a night will wake in the morning forgiven. And whoever recites Ha-Mim, the one in which there is smoke [Surah al-Dukhan], will wake in the morning forgiven." Its isnad is good. [Footnote: Musnad Abi Ya'la (11/93). In its isnad is Hisham ibn Ziyad, whom the imams declared weak. Ibn Hibban said: "He was among those who narrated fabrications from trustworthy narrators and reversed reports from reliable narrators, so that it comes to the mind of the listener that he was the one relied upon for them, and it is not permissible to argue with him." Al-Hasan did not hear from Abu Hurayrah; see the note on Abu Ya'la at his words "I heard."]

Ibn Hibban said in his Sahih: Muhammad ibn Ishaq ibn Ibrahim, client of Thaqif, narrated to us, al-Walid ibn Shuja' ibn al-Walid al-Sakuni narrated to us, my father narrated to us, Ziyad ibn Khaytamah narrated to us, Muhammad ibn Juhadah narrated to us, from al-Hasan, from Jundab ibn 'Abdullah, who said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "Whoever recites Ya-Sin on a night seeking the face of God, he will be forgiven." [Footnote: Sahih Ibn Hibban, no. (665), "Mawarid." Al-Hasan did not hear from Jundab, according to Abu Hatim.]

Imam Ahmad has also said: 'Arim narrated to us, Mu'tamir narrated to us, from his father, from a man, from his father, from Ma'qil ibn Yasar, may God be pleased with him, that the Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "al-Baqarah is the hump and peak of the Qur'an. With each of its verses, eighty angels descended. And [the verse] ﴿God, there is no deity except Him, the Living, the Sustainer﴾ [al-Baqarah 2:255] was brought out from beneath the Throne and joined to it, or: it was joined to Surah al-Baqarah.
